prompt:
Write the lyrics of a pop song about a breakup.

Write it as a working songwriter would, to be sung: lines that scan against a steady beat, a chorus that earns its repetition by meaning something slightly different each time it comes back, and verses that move a story forward through particular scenes, names, brands and street-level detail. Say the thing sideways: no line that states the feeling outright, no stock phrases, no word chosen only because it rhymes. Put one detail in each verse that only this story could contain.

Output only the lyrics, as plain lines with a blank line between sections: no title, no section labels, no chords, no commentary.
raw:
We're standing by the Shell on 42nd
You're tapping out a Camel on your phone
The sign is turning half your jacket green
You're telling me you're driving back alone
You still got my mechanic's number written
In blue ink on the back of your left hand
You climb into the Civic, lock the doors
And pull out past the taco stand

Roll the window up, the heater's broke
Take the bypass by the Dairy Queen
I don't need to know who's waiting up
Just tell me when you're off the street
Just tell me when you're off the street

It's Tuesday and your brother brought his Ford
You're carrying the speakers down the stairs
You left the plastic shower curtain hanging
And took the yellow cushions off the chairs
You're taping up a box of pans with duct tape
The silver roll we bought up at Menards
You ask me if I want the old transistor
That only gets the station for the Cards

Roll the window up, the heater's broke
Take the bypass by the Dairy Queen
I don't need to know who's waiting up
Just tell me when you're off the street
Just tell me when you're off the street

Your Lands' End catalogs keep showing up
I stack them by the radiator pipe
It's raining hard enough to flood the alley
And I keep checking if my screen is bright

Roll the window up, the heater's broke
Take the bypass by the Dairy Queen
I don't need to know who's waiting up
Just tell me when you're off the street
Just tell me when you're off the street
